newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo civil servants' wages to rise in 1997 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugo civil servants' wages to rise in 1997 - paper.

text.p: Yugoslavia's government plans to spend almost 476 million dinars ($90.75 million) on civil servants' wages in 1997, the Belgrade daily Vecernje novosti said on Wednesday.
Civil servants' monthly salaries will be calculated on a maximum base wage of 454 dinars, the paper said.

The prime minister, speakers of the Lower and Upper Houses of parliament and presidents of the Constitutional and Federal courts will have the same salaries, starting from 3,087 dinars and rising to 6,672 dinars by the end of 1997.
Fifteen ministers will receive a basic salary of 2,470 dinars per month, not including compensation for length of service, Vecernje Novosti said.

The average November salary in Yugoslavia was 787 dinars, with the Serbian average standing lower at 741 dinars. December's figures are not yet available. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
